blocks.text: Clear one mailbox from the sidebar on Mac

Apple's Mail User Guide describes the route plainly. To mark all unread messages in a mailbox as read, Control-click the mailbox in the Mail sidebar, then choose Mark All Messages As Read. You don't open a message. You don't select anything first. That is the whole task for one folder.

A mailbox is any folder in the sidebar. That includes Inbox, Sent, Drafts, and any folder you made yourself. The command works on one mailbox at a time, so plan a pass for each folder that still holds unread mail. If your Inbox is clear but a project folder isn't, that folder needs its own Control-click.
Learn the sidebar route first. It's the one Apple documents in its current Mail guide. It also matches what you see on screen, so it's easy to repeat each week.
Why mark all emails as read on Mac can go missing

The most common problem is that the command isn't in the menu at all. Apple's older Mail guide says the command appears only when the mailbox has at least one unread message. A fully read mailbox has nothing for it to act on, so the item doesn't show. That's the rule at work, not a broken menu.

The second most common problem is clicking the wrong place. Control-click the mailbox name in the sidebar. A right-click on a message in the list only acts on that message, so the mailbox command never appears. Check where your pointer sits, then open the menu again.
Mark selected messages as read instead

Sometimes you want to clear part of a mailbox, not all of it. Click the first message, then Shift-click the last one to select a range. Hold Command and click to add messages that aren't next to each other. Then choose Message > Mark as Read to clear the selection.

To select everything in the list, click inside the message list and press Command-A. Clean Email's guide describes this route: select all visible messages, then press Shift-Command-U. Apple's iCloud.com shortcut page lists Command-A as select all. Apple's Mac Mail shortcut page doesn't list one, so test it on your version before you rely on it.

blocks.text: Shift-Command-U and what it toggles

Shift-Command-U, shown as ⇧⌘U in menus, is the shortcut to know. Apple's Mac keyboard shortcut page lists it for marking emails as read or unread. It's a toggle, so the same key flips messages back and forth. Look at the status of the selection before you press it, or you may flip a batch the wrong way.

Apple notes that shortcuts can vary by language and keyboard layout. If the key does nothing on your keyboard, use Message > Mark as Read from the menu bar. The menu shows each shortcut beside its item, so you can confirm the key there.
Single messages and trackpad swipes

On a trackpad, swipe right with two fingers across one message. Then click Unread or Read. Apple's Mail guide describes this for a single message. It's quicker than a menu when you only need to fix one message.

Clearing unread mail matters because the time adds up. Microsoft's Work Trend Index puts the heaviest email users at 8.8 hours a week, though its data ends March 2023. Treat that as a rough signal, not a current benchmark.
Apple Mail also holds the largest share of email opens in the Litmus data. Litmus puts it at 76.56% for September 2026. That counts opens, not people, so read it as a share of opens.
Fix an unread count that won't drop

Sometimes the sidebar keeps a number after you've cleared everything. Clean Email suggests checking the unread count setting first. Open Mail > Settings > General. Set Unread Count to All Mailboxes, then look at the sidebar again.
If the count still looks wrong, select the mailbox and choose Mailbox > Rebuild. Clean Email lists this as the next fix. Give Mail a moment after you rebuild, then check the number again.
A worked example: clearing Newsletters and Inbox

Say your Newsletters folder holds a long run of unread promotions, and your Inbox holds a few messages that need replies. Start with Newsletters. Control-click it in the sidebar and choose Mark All Messages As Read. Those promotions leave your unread count without any reading from you.

Handle the Inbox in a different order. Select the messages that need replies first. Then Control-click Inbox and choose Mark All Messages As Read. Finally, select the reply messages again and choose Message > Mark as Unread, so they stay unread until you answer them.
Pulling the reply messages out first keeps them in view. Doing it the other way round means hunting for them later.

blocks.text: Mail on iCloud.com

Apple's iCloud.com shortcut list shows Command-A to select all and Shift-Command-U to mark read or unread on Mac. Apple doesn't document a mark-all command in iCloud Mail, so select messages and use the toggle there. Shortcut keys can vary by keyboard layout and language, as Apple notes.
If you're away from your Mac and reading mail in a browser, the iCloud.com page is the one to check. For the mark-all command itself, the Mac app is the place Apple documents it.
Which macOS version these steps cover

Apple's current Mail guide for this task is labeled macOS 26 in its web address. No wording change showed up in the macOS 27 entry of Apple's version selector. Menus still move between releases, so match names by meaning if yours differ.
An Apple Community answer posted in May 2026, on macOS 26.4, also lists Message > Mark as Read with ⇧⌘U. That fits the steps here, but it's a user answer, not an Apple guide.
What Apple documents and what it doesn't

Apple's documentation covers the sidebar route, the Message menu route, and the Shift-Command-U shortcut. The Mailbox menu route comes from third-party guides. How-To Geek's guide was published March 10, 2022, and doesn't name a macOS version. Treat the Mailbox menu item as optional, because it may not appear on your Mac.

Apple's Mail hub page doesn't carry steps for this task. It links to the Mail User Guides for Mac, iPhone, and iPad. When a step doesn't match your screen, open the Mac guide and search for the menu name.
Stop the same sender from refilling the pile

Clearing unread mail helps today, but one sender can refill the same folder by next week. If a single sender fills the mailbox, blocking that sender saves you the weekly cleanup. See [how to block a sender in Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/block-a-sender-in-apple-mail) for the steps.

faq.question: Does Mark All Messages As Read cover every account in Apple Mail?
faq.answer: No. Apple's guide describes the command for one mailbox at a time. Control-click each mailbox that has unread mail, such as Inbox and any folders you use, then check the sidebar again.

faq.question: Why doesn't Mark All Messages As Read show up in my menu?
faq.answer: Apple's older Mail guide says the command appears only when the mailbox has at least one unread message. If the mailbox is fully read, the item won't show. Also confirm you Control-clicked the mailbox in the sidebar, not a message.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to mark all messages as read in Apple Mail on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's Mac shortcut page lists Shift-Command-U to mark messages read or unread, but it doesn't list a mark-all key. Clean Email's guide selects everything with Command-A first, then uses Shift-Command-U. Shortcuts can vary by keyboard layout and language.

faq.question: Can I undo marking all messages as read?
faq.answer: Apple's guide doesn't describe an undo for the mailbox command. Select the messages you need, then choose Message > Mark as Unread. Shift-Command-U also toggles the selection back.

faq.question: Why does my unread count still show a number after I clear everything?
faq.answer: Clean Email suggests setting Mail > Settings > General > Unread Count to All Mailboxes. If the number is still off, select the mailbox and choose Mailbox > Rebuild.

faq.question: Do these steps work in Mail on iCloud.com?
faq.answer: Apple's iCloud.com shortcut page lists Command-A and Shift-Command-U for Mail on Mac. Apple doesn't document a mark-all command in iCloud Mail, so select messages and use the toggle.

faq.question: Are these steps the same on macOS 27?
faq.answer: Apple's current Mail guide for this task is labeled macOS 26. No wording change showed up in the macOS 27 entry of Apple's version selector, but menus can move between releases.

task: Mark all messages as read in Apple Mail on Mac
appliesTo: Apple Mail on Mac, steps from Apple's macOS 26 Mail guide
requirements: Apple Mail open on your Mac
At least one unread message in the mailbox you want to clear
A keyboard with Command and Shift keys for the shortcut route

steps.name: Open the mailbox in the sidebar
steps.text: Open Mail and look at the sidebar on the left. Find the mailbox that holds the unread messages, such as Inbox or a folder under one of your accounts. Work on one mailbox at a time, because the command applies to the mailbox you pick.
steps.tip: If you can't see the sidebar, the mailbox list is hidden. Bring it on screen before you continue.

steps.name: Control-click the mailbox name
steps.text: Hold the Control key and click the mailbox name. A right-click works too. Click the mailbox itself, not a message in the list. A short menu opens.
steps.tip: If the menu offers message options such as Reply, you clicked a message. Close it and try the mailbox name again.

steps.name: Choose Mark All Messages As Read
steps.text: In the short menu, choose Mark All Messages As Read. Mail marks every unread message in that mailbox as read. The item only appears when the mailbox has at least one unread message, so a fully read folder won't show it.

steps.name: Check the unread count
steps.text: Look at the number beside the mailbox name. It should no longer show unread mail for that mailbox. Then repeat the first three steps for each other mailbox that still has unread mail.

steps.name: Try the Mailbox menu if it appears
steps.text: Some third-party guides list Mailbox > Mark All Messages as Read in the menu bar, with a mailbox selected. Apple's Mail guide doesn't describe that route. If the item appears on your Mac, you can use it. If it doesn't, the sidebar route is the one Apple documents.
steps.tip: A missing item here is normal. Apple doesn't document it, so don't hunt for it.

steps.name: Mark selected messages as read
steps.text: For a handful of messages, click the first one, then Shift-click the last one to select a range. Hold Command and click to add single messages that aren't next to each other. Then choose Message > Mark as Read.
steps.tip: Shift-Command-U is a toggle. Check whether the selection is read or unread before you press it.

steps.name: Undo a mark as read
steps.text: To put messages back to unread, select them and choose Message > Mark as Unread. You can also press Shift-Command-U, which flips the selection. Apple's guide doesn't describe an undo for the mailbox command, so select the messages you need.

steps.name: Fix a stuck unread count
steps.text: Open Mail > Settings > General. Find Unread Count and set it to All Mailboxes. If the number still looks wrong, select the mailbox and choose Mailbox > Rebuild, then give Mail a moment.
steps.tip: Select the mailbox first, or the Rebuild command won't target the one you want.

troubleshooting.problem: Mark All Messages As Read is missing from the menu.
troubleshooting.fix: The mailbox probably has no unread messages, since Apple's older guide shows the command only when at least one is unread. Confirm you Control-clicked the mailbox name, not a message.
No messages are selected. Click the message list, press Command-A, then press Shift-Command-U. Clean Email describes this route.

troubleshooting.problem: The unread count still shows a number.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Mail > Settings > General and set Unread Count to All Mailboxes. If it's still off, select the mailbox and choose Mailbox > Rebuild.

troubleshooting.problem: The Mailbox menu has no Mark All Messages as Read item.
troubleshooting.fix: Apple's pages don't document that item, so it may not show on your Mac. Use the sidebar route, which Apple's Mail User Guide describes.

troubleshooting.problem: The shortcut does something different from the guide.
troubleshooting.fix: Apple notes that shortcuts can vary by language and keyboard layout. Use Message > Mark as Read from the menu bar instead, since the menu shows the shortcut beside it.

troubleshooting.problem: A shortcut flipped messages the wrong way.
troubleshooting.fix: Shift-Command-U toggles. Check the status of the selection first, or choose Message > Mark as Read or Mark as Unread directly.
